fields.why: The text ranks Hispanic adults above 'other racial/ethnic groups' and education and poverty levels against their counterparts, and Tables 1–2 give per-group values across 5 age groups.
Sex, disability and insurance are pairs and veteran status is not an SPD; education, FPL, race/ethnicity and age have 3 or more groups shown.

'Wald chi-squared tests ... to determine significant within-group differences' (SUDAAN) may be omnibus tests across the levels (a recognition cue, giving 'omnibus test' with resolves_to_finer), but every reported claim is a group vs its counterparts, so A's reading is defensible; age has no claim, so side by side holds and the flag is a weak alarm.

brief_issues: The brief does not say whether a survey 'Wald chi-square' stated once for 'within-group differences', with only group-vs-counterpart claims reported, is read as an omnibus test across the levels or as per-group tests; a rule (e.g. omnibus only when the test is stated as across the levels of a variable) would settle it.
